questions.question: Q: State Hubble's law and define each term.

points.text: v = H₀d, where v is recession velocity (km/s), H₀ is the Hubble constant (~70 km/s/Mpc), and d is distance (Mpc).

questions.question: Q: What is the cosmic microwave background?

points.text: Radiation from ~380,000 years after the Big Bang when the universe became transparent. It has been redshifted by expansion to microwave wavelengths at ~2.7 K.

questions.question: Q: How does redshift support the Big Bang theory?

points.text: Virtually all distant galaxies show redshift, indicating they are moving away from us — evidence the universe is expanding. If we rewind this expansion, everything converges to a single point ~13.8 billion years ago.

questions.question: Q: Explain Olbers' paradox and its resolution.

points.text: If the universe were infinite, static and eternal, the night sky should be bright (every line of sight ending on a star). It is dark because the universe is finite in age and expanding — distant starlight has not yet reached us, and redshift reduces energy.

questions.question: Q: How is the age of the universe estimated?

points.text: From the Hubble constant: t ≈ 1/H₀ ≈ 13.8 billion years. This is consistent with ages of the oldest stars and globular clusters.
